newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: UNHCR says may have to suspend Afghan programmes.
newsitem.headline: UNHCR says may have to suspend Afghan programmes.

text.p: The senior officer of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) in Kabul said on Saturday the agency's programmes would stay on hold until its staff returned and authorities had given guarantees of security.
"The situation will continue until we have a full staff and guarantees of security." Terry Pitzner, the officer in charge of the UNHCR Kabul office, told Reuters.

The UNHCR said on Wednesday it had put most of its programmes on hold until the security situation improved. "We have slowed down all programmes except the monitoring of refugees leaving Kabul." said Pitzner.
Pitzner said if there was no change in the situation, the UNHCR would suspend its programmes in Kabul.

"We did not do this by choice." said Pitzner. "We have no staff. We have seven women who have not been allowed to come in to work since the Taleban took over. We have had four more abducted and the rest of our staff requested to take leave, which we gave them."
When the Taleban took over Kabul in late September they banned women from the workplace. Pitzner says that to resume a full programme he must have his female staff.

Pitzner said that if the agency was forced to suspend its last remaining programme, the monitoring of refugee movements in and out of Kabul, it would severely affect the ability of the international community to respond to the needs of refugees.
"All the agencies use the information about the movement of refugees to find out where people are going and where the assistance is needed." said Pitzner.
UNHCR normally employs 22 people in Kabul. A spokesman for the UNHCR expressed concern for the arrested staff.

"We are extremely concerned about the safety of our arrested staffers, one of whom has been missing for almost four weeks. The rest of the staff are petrified," spokesman Rupert Colville said on Wednesday.
The UNHCR programmes that have been put on hold include a quilt-making project that aimed to make 50,000 quilts as part of a winter relief programme.
